run_metadata.coverage_summary: WebSearch-only discovery run under the same persistent hard egress block as prior runs: all direct HTTPS to buyer tender hosts is denied by the session network policy. WebFetch to www.tenders.gov.au, www.tenders.nsw.gov.au and www.vendorpanel.com.au each returned DNS ENOTFOUND again this run, so no buyer-originated detail page, RSS/JSON feed, API or tender document could be opened. Tier 1 (AusTender/DFAT, buy.nsw Opportunities Hub, Tenders VIC, QTenders/Queensland Procurement Solution, NT QTOL, Tenders WA, Tenders ACT) was swept via WebSearch snapshots; Tier 2 (universities, water corporations, port authorities) and Tier 3 (SAP Business Network Discovery, BAE Systems/Ivalua, Downer and Southern Ports on Felix) were sampled. Two currently-open, buyer-corroborated opportunities carried forward from recent runs remain open and were re-confirmed at headline level: the DFAT PNG Health Program ENABLE RFEOI (closing 1 Dec 2026) and the WA Government EOI for additional capacity at Kwinana Bulk Jetty (closing 23 Dec 2026). No new, independently-corroborated opportunity could be captured this run because live portals could not be opened; an NT 'AGC26-0118' consultancy lead surfaced in one search summary but could not be corroborated on a follow-up search and was deliberately excluded rather than fabricated. Two genuinely new buyer-originated sources were found (Downer Group and Southern Ports, both on the Felix platform).
gaps: HARD EGRESS BLOCK (unchanged, re-tested this run): all direct HTTPS to buyer tender hosts is denied by the session network policy. WebFetch to www.tenders.gov.au, www.tenders.nsw.gov.au and www.vendorpanel.com.au each returned DNS ENOTFOUND this run, so no buyer-originated detail page, RSS/JSON feed, API or tender document could be opened. To restore full discovery and deliverables extraction, these hosts (and the other Tier 1/2/3 tender hosts) need to be allowed in the session's network settings. Both captured tenders therefore remain headline-level and unverified against the live portal.

Tier 1: buy.nsw Opportunities Hub, QTenders/Queensland Procurement Solution, Tenders VIC and Tenders ACT could only be read through cached WebSearch snapshots; current open-tender lists filtered by publish/closing date could not be retrieved, so newly-published (last 24-48h) listings on those portals are likely under-captured.

Tier 3 (SAP Business Network Discovery / SAP Ariba Discovery): queried as mandatory, but the public posting board requires a free supplier login to view open Australian RFx; no authenticated session is available, so no individual corporate opportunity was publicly visible. Portal recorded in discovered_sources (access_method=portal-registration); no corporate tender fabricated.
Tier 3 invitation-only RFx (e.g. management-consultancy RFPs sent directly to shortlisted/panel suppliers) remain out of scope and undiscoverable by design, as noted in the task spec.

Unverified lead excluded: an NT tendersonline consultancy tender cited as 'AGC26-0118' (professional advisory services, closing 16/12/2026) appeared in one search summary but could not be confirmed on a targeted follow-up search (no listing with that exact number was found); excluded per the fidelity rule rather than recorded as a confirmed opportunity.
recommended_seed_additions: Downer Group — Working with Downer / vendor registration & prequalification on the Felix platform (felix.net); major Australian infrastructure, transport, utilities and facilities contractor issuing subcontract/supply packages.

Southern Ports (WA Government-owned port authority: Albany, Bunbury, Esperance) — supplier onboarding via the Felix platform; Tier 2 government business enterprise not previously in the known-source set.

tenders.jurisdiction: Australia — Commonwealth (program delivered in Papua New Guinea)
tenders.title: Managing Contractor — PNG Health Program ENABLE (Enhanced National Advice, Bilateral partnership, and Learning and Evidence)
tenders.buyer: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
tenders.category: Health systems strengthening / development program management (managing contractor)
tenders.procurement_type: RFEOI (Request for Expressions of Interest — stage 1 of a two-stage process)
tenders.description: DFAT is seeking a managing contractor to implement the PNG Health Program ENABLE, which supports delivery of the PNG–Australia Health Partnership Strategy 2024–2034 by strengthening selected national health systems and functions. This Request for Expressions of Interest is the first stage of a two-stage procurement, intended to establish a shortlist of capable organisations.
tenders.deliverables_summary: A managing contractor to implement the ENABLE health investment in Papua New Guinea from 2027 — providing enhanced national (health) advice, supporting the Australia–PNG bilateral partnership, and running a learning-and-evidence function to strengthen selected PNG national health systems and functions. This RFEOI stage asks respondents to demonstrate capability to shortlist for the subsequent RFT stage.
key_deliverables: Managing-contractor services to implement the PNG Health Program ENABLE from 2027
Enhanced national health advice to support PNG health systems
Support to the Australia–PNG bilateral health partnership
Learning and evidence function (monitoring, learning, evidence generation)
tenders.scope_of_work: Per DFAT's published development page and the PNG ENABLE concept note: deliver a managing-contractor model to support implementation of the PNG–Australia Health Partnership Strategy 2024–2034, strengthening selected national systems and functions. Full scope sits in the RFEOI documents on AusTender, which could not be opened this run.
tenders.eligibility: Open RFEOI to establish a shortlist of capable organisations (stage 1 of a two-stage process).
tenders.contract_term: Initial 5-year term from 2027, with possible extension up to 2037
tenders.briefing: DFAT states it will hold an industry briefing during the RFEOI period (date not published in the sources read this run).
tenders.delivery_location: Papua New Guinea (managed by DFAT, Commonwealth of Australia)
tenders.detail_source: DFAT development business-notification page (dfat.gov.au) and the published PNG ENABLE concept note (scope/term); ATM id, closing date/time and value corroborated via the DevelopmentAid aggregator — not opened on AusTender directly.
tenders.reasoning: Carried forward from the 2026-11-23 run and re-confirmed still open via WebSearch (DFAT Development Procurement Pipeline snapshot shows DFAT-1113 closing 1 Dec 2026). DFAT's own published development page corroborates the RFEOI nature, two-stage process, scope and 2027 start / up-to-2037 term. ATM id, closing date and indicative value were corroborated via the DevelopmentAid aggregator used only as a discovery/corroboration signal; the buyer-originated source recorded is DFAT/AusTender.
tenders.notes: Headline-only, re-confirmed open on 2026-11-24. Egress block prevented opening the AusTender ATM record and RFEOI documents, so closing time, exact value, industry-briefing date and evaluation criteria are from an aggregator or the concept note and need verification on AusTender. value (AUD 85M) is an aggregator figure, not confirmed on the DFAT/AusTender notice. Now within 7 days of closing — status updated to closing-soon.

tenders.source_name: Government of Western Australia — Media Statement / Tenders WA
tenders.title: Expression of Interest — Additional Trade Capacity at Kwinana Bulk Jetty
tenders.buyer: Government of Western Australia (Ports portfolio / Fremantle Ports)
tenders.category: Ports and maritime infrastructure / market sounding
tenders.description: The WA Government has called for expressions of interest from industry to explore additional trade capacity at Kwinana Bulk Jetty, a strategically important piece of State port infrastructure. Announced via a Government of WA media statement on 6 November 2026 (Ports Minister Stephen Dawson), the EOI seeks market interest from proponents in using or expanding capacity at the jetty.
tenders.deliverables_summary: Proponents are invited to register interest in developing or utilising additional trade/throughput capacity at Kwinana Bulk Jetty. The Government's stated outcome is to test market appetite and options for expanding the jetty's trade capacity. Full scope, respondent obligations and any works/services split were not published in the media statement and sit in the EOI documents on Tenders WA, which could not be opened this run.
tenders.eligibility: Open market sounding — industry participants with an interest in additional trade capacity at Kwinana Bulk Jetty.
tenders.submission_method: Via Tenders WA (EOI record); registration details in the EOI documents (not opened this run)
tenders.delivery_location: Kwinana Bulk Jetty, Kwinana / Cockburn Sound, Western Australia
tenders.reasoning: Carried forward from the 2026-11-23 run and still open (closing 23 Dec 2026). Originally discovered via WebSearch surfacing the official Government of WA media statement (wa.gov.au, dated 6 Nov 2026); corroborated by Westport WA and The DCN maritime coverage. Buyer-originated (WA Government); the formal EOI is expected on Tenders WA. Distinct from the separate Westport/Fremantle Ports 'Kwinana Bulk Terminal Redevelopment — Marine Infrastructure' Design & Construct EOI (July 2026).
tenders.notes: Headline-only, still open as at 2026-11-24. Egress block prevented opening the Tenders WA EOI record and documents, so tender_id, closing time, submission mechanics and detailed scope are null/unverified. Closing date (23 Dec 2026) and publish date (6 Nov 2026) are from the WA Government media statement. Must be confirmed on the live Tenders WA portal.
